name: Thoracolumbar fascia, posterior layer

bony_attachments.landmark: lumbar and lower thoracic spinous processes

function: Most superficial of the three TLF layers, enclosing the erector spinae posteriorly; blends laterally with the aponeuroses of latissimus dorsi and gluteus maximus, forming a documented myofascial force-transmission pathway linking the contralateral latissimus dorsi and gluteus maximus across the lumbosacral junction during gait (part of the same functional coupling Vleeming separately describes as sacroiliac 'self-bracing'/form-and-force-closure, though that exact term is not used in this specific 1995 paper).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Vleeming A, Pool-Goudzwaard AL, Stoeckart R, van Wingerden JP, Snijders CJ (1995) Spine 20(7):753-758 -- the posterior layer of the thoracolumbar fascia's role transferring load between the spine and legs via its latissimus dorsi/gluteus maximus attachments

name: Thoracolumbar fascia, middle layer

bony_attachments.landmark: tips of the lumbar transverse processes

function: Separates the erector spinae (posterior layer) from quadratus lumborum (anterior layer); laterally, all three TLF layers fuse into a single dense band that becomes the origin of transversus abdominis and internal oblique.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone

name: Thoracolumbar fascia, anterior layer (quadratus lumborum fascia)

bony_attachments.landmark: anterior surfaces of the lumbar transverse processes

function: Thinnest of the three layers, covering the anterior surface of quadratus lumborum; its thickened superior border forms the lateral arcuate ligament (lumbocostal arch), which gives partial origin to the diaphragm. Not to be confused with the lumbocostal ligament (ligament of Henle), a distinct structure lying posterior to quadratus lumborum that blends with the middle layer rather than this one.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Rectus sheath
function: Formed by the interweaving aponeuroses of external oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis, enclosing rectus abdominis in anterior and posterior laminae; below the arcuate line (classically described as roughly midway between umbilicus and pubis, though cadaveric studies find its true position more variable, often closer to the umbilicus) all three aponeuroses pass anterior to rectus abdominis, leaving only transversalis fascia posteriorly -- a clinically important discontinuity near/below which Spigelian and other abdominal wall hernias occur (within the 'Spigelian belt' along the linea semilunaris, not exactly at the line itself).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Linea alba
function: Midline fibrous raphe formed by the decussating fibers of the left and right rectus sheaths; avascular and relatively thin, making it the conventional surgical access line for laparotomy and a documented site of acquired weakness (diastasis recti, e.g. postpartum).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Inguinal ligament (Poupart's ligament)
compartment_contents: external_oblique_r_main (lowest fibers, rolled under to form the ligament)
function: Thickened, rolled-under inferior border of the external oblique aponeurosis, spanning ASIS to pubic tubercle; forms the floor of the inguinal canal and the anterior boundary between the abdomen and thigh (structures deep to it -- iliopsoas, femoral vessels, femoral nerve -- pass into the thigh beneath it).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Transversalis fascia
function: Part of the continuous endoabdominal fascial envelope lining the abdominal wall deep to transversus abdominis; forms the deep inguinal ring where it evaginates around the spermatic cord/round ligament, and is the sole posterior covering of rectus abdominis below the arcuate line.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone

name: Diaphragmatic fascia (phrenicopleural/phrenicoperitoneal)
function: Thin fascial covering on both surfaces of the diaphragm, continuous superiorly with the endothoracic fascia (parietal pleura's fascial backing) and inferiorly with transversalis fascia -- part of the same continuous somatic fascial envelope described by Stecco as running the length of the trunk wall.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone

name: Endothoracic fascia

bony_attachments.landmark: internal surface of the rib cage

function: Thin areolar fascial layer lining the internal surface of the thoracic wall deep to the intercostal muscles, continuous with the diaphragmatic fascia below -- the thoracic-cage counterpart of the abdomen's transversalis fascia in Stecco's continuous-envelope model.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone

name: Pelvic diaphragm fascia (superior/inferior fascia of levator ani)

bony_attachments.landmark: tendinous arch of levator ani (arcus tendineus levator ani)

function: Fascial coverings on the superior (pelvic) and inferior (perineal) surfaces of levator ani/coccygeus, continuous with the obturator internus fascia at the tendinous arch that gives levator ani part of its origin.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Gluteal fascia

bony_attachments.landmark: lateral border and the sacrotuberous ligament

function: Splits to enclose gluteus maximus and covers gluteus medius as a single dense layer. Continuous below with the fascia lata and above with the posterior thoracolumbar fascia -- one of the links in the posterior oblique sling between latissimus dorsi and the contralateral gluteus maximus.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone

name: Latissimus dorsi aponeurosis

bony_attachments.landmark: posterior third of the iliac crest

function: The broad tendinous origin of latissimus dorsi, fused with the posterior layer of the thoracolumbar fascia. Transmits load from the arm across the midline to the contralateral gluteus maximus.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone

name: External oblique aponeurosis

bony_attachments.landmark: anterior iliac crest and pubic tubercle
xiphoid process, via the linea alba

function: Passes entirely ANTERIOR to rectus abdominis at every level. Its lower free border rolls back on itself as the inguinal ligament, and it forms the anterior wall of the inguinal canal.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Internal oblique aponeurosis

bony_attachments.landmark: iliac crest and the lateral inguinal ligament

function: Splits around rectus abdominis above the arcuate line and passes entirely anterior to it below -- the split that creates the arcuate line itself, below which the posterior rectus sheath is absent.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Transversus abdominis aponeurosis
function: Posterior to rectus abdominis above the arcuate line, anterior to it below. The plane between transversus abdominis and internal oblique carries the thoracoabdominal nerves and is the target of the TAP block.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Camper's fascia (fatty layer of superficial fascia)
function: The fatty superficial layer of the anterior abdominal wall, continuous over the inguinal ligament into the thigh and over the perineum. It is the layer whose thickness dominates abdominal wall ultrasound depth.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone

name: Scarpa's fascia (membranous layer of superficial fascia)

bony_attachments.landmark: attaches to the fascia lata just below the inguinal ligament

function: The membranous layer beneath Camper's. It does NOT cross into the thigh -- it fuses with the fascia lata a fingerbreadth below the inguinal ligament -- but it does continue into the perineum as Colles' fascia. That attachment pattern is what confines extravasated urine from a ruptured bulbar urethra to the perineum, scrotum and abdominal wall while sparing the thigh.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone

name: Colles' fascia (superficial perineal fascia)

bony_attachments.landmark: ischiopubic rami and the posterior border of the perineal membrane

function: The perineal continuation of Scarpa's fascia, closing the superficial perineal pouch. Its lateral and posterior attachments are the anatomical boundary that directs urinary extravasation forwards and upwards rather than into the thigh or ischioanal fossa.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Psoas fascia

bony_attachments.landmark: transverse processes and vertebral bodies L1-L5

compartment_contents: lumbar plexus branches within the muscle
function: Encloses psoas as a closed sleeve continuous with the iliac fascia. Tuberculous or pyogenic vertebral infection tracks inside this sleeve to point below the inguinal ligament as a psoas abscess. The same plane is the target of the lumbar plexus and fascia iliaca blocks.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Iliac fascia

bony_attachments.landmark: iliac crest and the arcuate line of the ilium

function: Covers iliacus and roofs the femoral nerve. The fascia iliaca compartment block deposits anaesthetic beneath this sheet to reach the femoral and lateral femoral cutaneous nerves together, which is why it works for hip fracture pain without needing to find the nerve itself.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Renal (Gerota's) fascia
function: Anterior and posterior leaves enclosing the kidney and perirenal fat, open inferiorly. That open inferior margin is why perinephric collections and blood track downwards towards the pelvis, and the plane surgeons stay outside of in radical nephrectomy.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Nuchal ligament (ligamentum nuchae)

bony_attachments.landmark: external occipital protuberance and median nuchal line

function: The midline fibro-elastic septum of the posterior neck, serving as the medial attachment for trapezius, splenius capitis and rhomboid minor, and substituting for the short cervical spinous processes. Its elasticity assists recovery from neck flexion.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Erector spinae aponeurosis
function: The broad tendinous origin of erector spinae, blending with the posterior thoracolumbar fascia. The plane deep to it is the target of the erector spinae plane (ESP) block, which spreads craniocaudally over several segments.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone
